resolution: Inspected the bundled Zig 0.16 Io implementation to explain nonblocking behavior. Zig moved from caller-managed EAGAIN polling to an injected structured-concurrency interface: Io.concurrent returns a Future while guaranteeing a unit of concurrency, with Group/Select, await/cancel, cancellation points, and timeouts. std.process.Init.io is a properly initialized Threaded backend using a worker pool; the repo's global_single_threaded shortcut disables that concurrency. Also confirmed the 0.16 Linux Uring/Evented backend still marks TCP listen/connect/accept/read/write unavailable, making a narrow raw readiness adapter defensible for an existing frame loop, but not a copied std.net compatibility layer.
